verdict.rationale: mParticle documents Warehouse Sync, which ingests existing tables from Snowflake, Redshift, BigQuery and Databricks via an API, SQL reference and data mapping, and audiences can then be connected to outputs for activation. This lets warehouse data be activated without re-instrumenting collection. However, the evidence describes ingesting (copying) warehouse data into mParticle rather than defining models and audiences natively on the warehouse tables. A 'Composable Audiences' page exists, but the pack gives only its title, so no warehouse-native audience definition is evidenced. Missing for 10: evidence of defining models and audiences directly on warehouse tables without copying data into mParticle, details of Composable Audiences, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a data engineer, I can run warehouse-native: define models and audiences on tables already in my warehouse and activate them without re-collecting the data (reverse ETL)

citations.quote: Warehouse Sync ingests data from your own warehouse into mParticle — documented setup flows cover Snowflake, Amazon Redshift, Google BigQuery, and Databricks
Once you have created an audience, you must connect it to an audience output where you can activate it.
